native_result.query: How does the consideration of academic characteristics alter the effects of Socioeconomic Status and race on BA degree completion?
native_result.HypoA: When academic characteristics are considered, the effect of SES on BA degree completion is reduced and the effect of race is enlarged.
native_result.HypoB: Socioeconomic status is a strong correlate of educational attainment (highest grade completed by 1979), but much of its association operates through academic characteristics: adding the ASVAB achievement composite and class-rank percentile attenuates mother's-education coefficients by ~39-44%, father's-education by ~50-62%, and eliminates the family-income effect, across OLS, ordinal-logit and complete-case/imputation specifications. By contrast, racial/ethnic differences in attainment are NOT attenuated by academic controls: conditional on achievement, Black and Hispanic respondents completed MORE schooling than comparable non-Black non-Hispanic respondents, indicating that the racial gap in attainment is concentrated in measured achievement itself rather than in attainment conditional on achievement. The sparse Firth BA (grade>=16) models replicate this directional pattern with very wide uncertainty.
native_result.WorkflowB: Cleaning (code 95->missing; income top-coded at 75,001 with indicator; log income); SES = mother's & father's education, log income 1979, family size; race dummies (ref=non-Black non-Hispanic); controls = sex, age 1979. Model 2 adds z-standardized 4-section ASVAB composite and class-rank percentile (+ missing indicator). Same-sample complete-case comparison (n=7,506) plus median-imputation-with-indicators sensitivity (n=12,532); outcomes: (i) OLS grade continuous (HC3), ordinal logit; (ii) Firth-penalized logistic for grade>=16 (24 events, quasi-separation caveat); (iii) standard logistic grade>=13 (1,015 events). Attenuation = (b1-b2)/b1*100; VIF all <2.0.
